correctness.rationale: The Fourier basis product has exactly one nonzero partner; zero products force derivations diagonal, and the remaining Leibniz equations become t(-a)=-t(a), t(2a)=2t(a). Orbit stabilizers for elements of exact additive order m are trivial within H_m, yielding the phi(m)/|H_m| count and exact scalar-character consistency tests. Commutativity follows from common Fourier diagonality; rank preservation under extension descends to K. A fully independent basis coefficient elimination checks all selected (n,p), and all 11^3 coefficient tests confirm the explicit characteristic-three derivation. Arbitrary n follows by proof, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: The nearest complete primary source (Elhamdadi et al., 2021) proves only characteristic-zero all-odd rigidity plus modular cases of order at most six. This all-odd, characteristic-prime-to-order divisor formula and its order-eleven characteristic-three exception are not subsumed by those statements. Sangare–Ta (2026) treats idempotents/automorphisms/commutators, not this modular derivation classification. The Fourier approach of Elhamdadi–Ta–Virgin (2026) concerns idempotents; its full text remains an explicit originality risk. Published-record and general literature queries returned no matching claim, but absence of retrieval is not a global novelty proof.

value.rationale: The precise derivation Lie algebra of odd dihedral quandle algebras in positive characteristic, prime to order, is a natural gap after the 2021 char-zero theorem and small modular tables. The all-order arithmetic classification and first order-eleven modular jump genuinely distinguish infinitesimal behavior by the multiplicative order of 2 and inversion; this is structural rather than a small ad hoc instance. It yields an explicit family-level dimension invariant in an active algebraic literature context.
